Spec review companion · #112 · snapshot 11f41cb · 2026-10-27

Use the remote branch when the default branch has no local ref

Read the open sections in about ten minutes. Everything closed is a look-up. A file:line chip jumps to the source line at the bottom, for when a claim needs checking.

Bug #112

The change

A branch review fails in a clone that has no local default branch, such as one made with git clone -b feature. The plugin takes main from origin/HEAD and passes it to git merge-base, which does not know it. assessment:23

The fix checks refs/heads/<name> and uses origin/<name> when that local branch does not exist. fix:10

2code files fix:18
5tests added fix:19
6checks passed test:19
0checks failed test:22
1deviation fix:61

Root cause

detectDefaultBranch assumes that the branch origin/HEAD names exists as a local branch. assessment:52

Remediation

One show-ref check, the same rule the candidate loop already uses. The loop and the error stay. assessment:59

How it works

Examples

These are the tests and the reproduction that ran. test:19

git clone -b feature

Base origin/main, label "branch diff against origin/main". The issue's own case; it failed on main. fix:34

Single-branch clone

With main fetched and origin/HEAD set: the same result. The issue names this shape. fix:38

Local main exists

Base main, as before. Guards the local case. fix:41

origin/HEAD points at a missing ref

Base origin/gone, then merge-base fails, as today. fix:43

Name main&branch-helper&x, remote only

Base origin/main&branch-helper&x; the .cmd helper does not run, so the name reaches git literally. fix:45

# Bug Assessment: a branch review fails when the default branch exists only on the remote - **Slug**: 112-use-remote-default-branch- **Created**: 2026-10-27- **Source**: pasted text (GitHub issue #112)- **Verdict**: valid- **Severity**: medium ## Report (verbatim or summarized) Summarized from #112. `detectDefaultBranch` (`plugins/copilot/scripts/lib/git.mjs`) reads`refs/remotes/origin/HEAD`. When it points at `origin/main`, the function returns `main` and doesnot check that `refs/heads/main` exists. The candidate loop below it checks the local branch, thenthe remote one, but it runs only when `origin/HEAD` is not set. `git clone -b feature <origin>`gives `origin/HEAD`, `origin/main` and a local `feature` only. `resolveReviewTarget` then returns`baseRef: "main"`, and `collectReviewContext` fails with`merge-base HEAD main: exit=128: fatal: Not a valid object name main`. The issue asks that the basebe `origin/<name>` unless `refs/heads/<name>` exists, with a test, a README difference line, and apatch release. ## Symptom A branch review (`/copilot:review` or `/copilot:adversarial-review` on a clean tree, or with`--scope branch`) in a clone that has no local default branch fails at `git merge-base`. Expected:the review runs against `origin/<name>`. ## Reproduction Reproduced on 2026-10-27 with the code on `main` (757e52b), from a Node script outside the repo: 1. Make a repo with `main` (one commit) and `feature` (one more commit), with `main` checked out.2. `git clone -b feature <that repo> clone`. In the clone, `git symbolic-ref   refs/remotes/origin/HEAD` prints `refs/remotes/origin/main`, and the only local branch is   `refs/heads/feature`.3. In the clone, `resolveReviewTarget(clone, {})` returns `baseRef: "main"`.4. `collectReviewContext(clone, target)` throws `... merge-base HEAD main: exit=128: fatal: Not a   valid object name main`. ## Suspected Code Paths - `plugins/copilot/scripts/lib/git.mjs:114-121` (`detectDefaultBranch`): the `origin/HEAD` branch  returns the bare name with no check of `refs/heads/<name>`.- `plugins/copilot/scripts/lib/git.mjs:123-133`: the candidate loop already checks the local  branch, then `origin/<candidate>`. It runs only when `origin/HEAD` is not set.- `plugins/copilot/scripts/lib/git.mjs:199` and `:216` (`resolveReviewTarget`): the two callers.  The base goes into the label and into `merge-base HEAD <base>` at `git.mjs:90`.- Upstream codex-plugin-cc v1.0.6 (`scripts/lib/git.mjs:94-116`, read from the installed Codex  plugin) has the same code. ## Root Cause Hypothesis `detectDefaultBranch` takes the name that `origin/HEAD` points to and assumes that a local branch ofthat name exists. A clone made with `-b <other branch>`, a single-branch clone, and many CIcheckouts have only the remote-tracking ref, so the bare name is not a valid object and`git merge-base` fails. Confidence: high (reproduced, and the code path is short). ## Proposed Remediation **Preferred**: in the `origin/HEAD` branch of `detectDefaultBranch`, after the prefix is removed,run `git show-ref --verify --quiet refs/heads/<name>` with the existing `git` helper (no shell, sothe name is passed literally). Return `<name>` when it exists, and `origin/<name>` when it doesnot. This is the rule that the candidate loop already uses. The loop and the error stay as theyare. **Alternatives**:- Always return `origin/<name>`: one line less, but a clone with a local default branch would  review against the remote ref, which can be older or newer than the local one. The issue asks  for `<name>` in that case. **Files likely to change**:- `plugins/copilot/scripts/lib/git.mjs` (and its "Changed from upstream" header comment)- `tests/git.test.mjs` (and its "Changed from upstream" header comment)- `README.md` ("Differences from the Codex plugin")- `plugins/copilot/CHANGELOG.md` and the version files (`npm run bump-version -- 1.0.21`) **Tests to add or update**:- The source is a temp repo with `main` (one commit) and `feature` (one more commit), with `main`  checked out, so that a clone's `origin/HEAD` points at `origin/main`.- A clone made with `git clone -b feature`: the test checks that `origin/HEAD` and `origin/main`  exist and `refs/heads/main` does not. Then `resolveReviewTarget` (with no scope and with  `scope: "branch"`) returns `baseRef: "origin/main"` and the label `branch diff against  origin/main`, and `collectReviewContext` gives a branch diff with the feature change. This test  fails on the current code.- A clone made with `git clone --single-branch -b feature`, then `git fetch origin  main:refs/remotes/origin/main` and `git remote set-head origin main`, so it has the same refs:  the same checks. This is the single-branch clone that the issue names.- The `-b feature` clone after `git branch main origin/main`: the base is `main` and the label  `branch diff against main`. This passes on the current code too; it guards the local case  against a regression.- An `origin/HEAD` that points at `refs/remotes/origin/gone`, which does not exist, with no local  `gone`: the base is `origin/gone`, and `collectReviewContext` fails with an error that names  `merge-base HEAD origin/gone`. This pins today's failure, which stays as it is (see "Risks &  Considerations"); it is not a requirement.- The existing test for a default branch name with special characters (it has a local branch)  must still pass, so the name still reaches git literally. A remote-only variant of it (it checks  out `feature/test`, then deletes the local branch of that name with `git branch -D`, run with  `shell: false`) gives `origin/main&branch-helper&x` and creates no helper file, so the new  `show-ref` call and the `origin/<name>` return pass the name literally too.- The header comment of `tests/git.test.mjs` names the remote-only default-branch tests. **Checks**: `npm ci --include=dev`, `npm run build`, `npm test`, `npm run check-version` and`claude plugin validate .` must pass before the PR. ## Risks & Considerations - A label changes: the review says "branch diff against origin/main" in such a clone, where today  it fails. A clone with the local branch keeps "main".- An `origin/HEAD` that points at a ref that does not exist (a dangling symbolic ref) still fails at  `merge-base`, now with `origin/<name>` in the message. That is the same failure as today, and the  issue does not ask to change it.- A `show-ref` that fails for any reason counts as "no local branch", as in the candidate loop.  The base is then `origin/<name>`, which `merge-base` checks.- `origin/<name>` is the remote-tracking ref as of the last fetch. The plugin does not fetch, as  today.- The difference from upstream is a correctness change; the README section gets one bullet. ## Open Questions None. ## Constitution Check - **I. Upstream parity**: met. The function name and its candidate loop stay. The one change from  upstream is a correctness difference, listed in the README section "Differences from the Codex  plugin" with its reason, and in the "Changed from upstream" header comments of `git.mjs` and  `tests/git.test.mjs`.- **II. Only reviewed code**: met. One `show-ref` call written here, after the candidate loop's own  check; no new dependency.- **III. Copilot CLI through documented interfaces only**: met. No change to how Copilot is called.- **IV. Safe by default**: met. A read-only `git show-ref`, started with no shell; the name is passed  as one argument.- **V. Cross-platform**: met. Plain git refs and a local clone in a temp folder; CI runs the test on  Ubuntu, macOS and Windows.- **VI. Tested, including failure paths**: met. Tests for the remote-only case (a `-b` clone and a  single-branch clone, auto and branch scope), the local case, and an `origin/HEAD` that points at a  missing ref; the special-character test and the no-default-branch error test stay.  Patch release with its `CHANGELOG.md` entry, and the release run after the merge.

# Bug Fix: a branch review fails when the default branch exists only on the remote - **Slug**: 112-use-remote-default-branch- **Fixed**: 2026-10-27- **Assessment**: ./assessment.md- **Status**: applied ## Summary `detectDefaultBranch` now checks `refs/heads/<name>` for the name that `origin/HEAD` gives, andreturns `origin/<name>` when that local branch does not exist. A branch review in a clone with nolocal default branch then compares against the remote-tracking ref, and `git merge-base` works. ## Changes | File | Change | Notes ||------|--------|-------|| `plugins/copilot/scripts/lib/git.mjs` | modified | One `show-ref --verify --quiet refs/heads/<name>` call in the `origin/HEAD` branch; a header comment line for the upstream difference || `tests/git.test.mjs` | added tests | Five tests and four small helpers; a header comment line || `README.md` | modified | One bullet in "Differences from the Codex plugin" (correctness) || `plugins/copilot/CHANGELOG.md` | modified | `### 1.0.21` entry || `package.json`, `package-lock.json`, `plugins/copilot/.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` | modified | `npm run bump-version -- 1.0.21` | ## Diff Highlights (optional) ```jsconst name = remoteHead.replace("refs/remotes/origin/", "");const local = git(cwd, ["show-ref", "--verify", "--quiet", `refs/heads/${name}`]);return local.status === 0 ? name : `origin/${name}`;``` ## Tests Added or Updated - `tests/git.test.mjs` "a branch review in a clone with no local default branch runs against  origin/<name>": a `git clone -b feature` clone has `origin/HEAD` and `origin/main` but no  `refs/heads/main`; with no scope and with `scope: "branch"`, the base is `origin/main`, the label  is `branch diff against origin/main`, and the context holds the feature change.- "a branch review in a single-branch clone runs against origin/<name> once the default branch is  fetched": `--single-branch -b feature`, then `fetch origin main:refs/remotes/origin/main` and  `remote set-head origin main`; the same checks.- "a clone with a local default branch still reviews against <name>": after  `git branch main origin/main`, the base is `main` and the label `branch diff against main`.- "an origin/HEAD that points at a missing ref gives origin/<name> and fails at merge-base": pins  today's failure for a dangling `origin/HEAD`, with the error text.- "a default branch name with special characters is passed to git literally when only the remote  has it": `main&branch-helper&x` only as a remote ref; the base is `origin/main&branch-helper&x`,  the branch diff is collected, and the `.cmd` helper does not run. ## Local Verification - With the code on `main` put back for a moment, the four remote-only tests fail and the local-case  test passes; with the fix, all pass.- Commands run: `npm ci --include=dev` (0 vulnerabilities), `npm run build` (pass), `npm test`  (442 tests: 418 pass, 24 skipped, 0 fail), `npm run check-version` (1.0.21),  `claude plugin validate .` (pass).- Manual checks: the reproduction script from `assessment.md` ("Reproduction") failed on `main`  with `merge-base HEAD main: exit=128`. ## Deviations from Assessment - 2026-10-27, review round 1 (`code-review`): the assessment's root cause says that a single-branch  clone and many CI checkouts have this shape. They do not: `actions/checkout` and a plain  `git clone --single-branch -b <branch>` set no `origin/HEAD`, so they take the candidate loop,  as before. The fix does not change them. The README and the 1.0.21 `CHANGELOG.md` entry name only  a clone such as `git clone -b <other branch>`; the single-branch test fetches the default branch  and sets `origin/HEAD` by hand, as the assessment says. ## Follow-ups - Upstream codex-plugin-cc v1.0.6 has the same code (`scripts/lib/git.mjs:94-116`); the owner may  report it upstream.
